'''Zanaris''', also known as the '''Lost City''', is the home of the [[Fairy (race)|fairies]] and is the moon of [[Gielinor]].{{CiteNPC|npc=Konar quo Maten|quote=Zanaris is the moon of this world.|loc=Slayer area descriptions}}{{CiteNews|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/qa-summary-07042022?oldschool=1|title=Q&A Summary 07/04/2022|newsdate=12 April 2022|quote=Yep, the moon is called Zanaris and the city there is also called Zanaris.|notes=Question #31}} Accessed during the [[Lost City]] quest, the settlement is notable for bearing several amenities, such as a marketplace to buy a [[dragon longsword]], and the highly useful [[fairy ring]] transportation system.

The entrance to Zanaris is located in the [[Shed (Lumbridge Swamp)|shed]] in [[Lumbridge Swamp]].

==History==
Zanaris is an extremely old place, and is rumoured to be the nexus of all planes.{{CiteNPC|npc=Co-ordinator|quote=Zanaris is an extremely old place, it was here long before we fairyfolk came to live here. In fact it is rumoured to be the nexus of all planes.|loc=Fairytale II - Cure a Queen|notes=|name=}} When the [[Fairy (race)|fairies]] first inhabited Zanaris, they discovered it had many dormant magic properties, including the ability to jump between planes through a powerful portal that had been sealed for centuries. The Fairy Queen harnessed its magic and used it to create the [[fairy ring]]s,{{CiteNPC|npc=Co-ordinator|quote=When we arrived here we found many of the magical properties of this place to be dormant. One of these was the ability to jump between planes using a powerful portal that had been sealed for centuries. The Fairy Queen harnessed that magic and created the fairy rings, these are not as powerful as the original portal would have been, but are very effective nonetheless.|loc=Fairytale II - Cure a Queen|notes=|name=}} which the fairies used to help manage the seasons and weather of [[Gielinor]], as well as to collect teeth.{{CiteNPC|npc=Co-ordinator|quote=Sorry, I don't have time for idle chit-chat, I need to send an Autumn Fairy off to Burthorpe!|loc=|notes=|name=}}{{CiteNPC|npc=Co-ordinator|quote=Sorry, I don't have time to stop, I need to send a Weather Fairy off to Etceteria!|loc=|notes=|name=}}{{CiteNPC|npc=Co-ordinator|quote=Sorry, I don't have time to talk, I need to send a Tooth Fairy to visit Sarah-Jane!|loc=|notes=|name=}}

Recently, the [[Fairy Godfather]] and his [[Fairy Mafia]] has staged a coup. The Godfather attacked the Fairy Queen and drained much of her magic essence, and in her absence, kidnapped and attacked many of the fairies, as well as bringing over an army of [[ork (Zanaris)|orks]] into Zanaris.{{CiteNPC|npc=Fairy Nuff|quote=When I noticed that lots of my friends were missing, when I asked him about them he said they were off working for him and then he threatened to have his bodyguards pull my wings off!|loc=|notes=|name=}}{{CiteNPC|npc=Fairy Nuff|quote=He wants to rule Zanaris instead of the Fairy Queen. The latest fairies to arrive have even reported that he has invited all sorts of monsters to the Lost City.|loc=|notes=|name=}} The Fairy Queen was taken to a safe [[Fairy Resistance Hideout|hideout]], and an [[player character|adventurer]] was able to help her recover. She and the other fairies are currently planning to retake Zanaris from the Fairy Godfather.

==Transportation==
The [[fairy ring]] code for the main portal in Zanaris is {{Fairycode|BKS}}. Zanaris can also be accessed by wielding a [[dramen staff]] or [[lunar staff]] and entering the small hut in the middle of [[Lumbridge Swamp]], north-west of the [[Mining]] [[tutor]], [[Monlum]], in the [[East Lumbridge Swamp mine]]. Players can also gain access via [[The Abyss]] to the [[Cosmic Altar]]. 

There is a one-way fairy ring to [[Al Kharid]] bank from the market area.

==Quests==
The [[Lost City]] quest is a pre-requisite to visiting Zanaris. Both [[Fairytale I - Growing Pains|Fairytale Part I]] and [[Fairytale II - Cure a Queen|Part II]] naturally require visits to the land of the fairies.

==Notable features==
===Fairy rings===
*The [[fairy ring]] is located south of the water fountains and west of the farm field (code {{Fairycode|bks}}). Activating the ring while carrying a [[dramen staff]] or [[lunar staff]] will open a combination window to enter a code to go to other fairy rings elsewhere in [[Gielinor]].
*The other two original fairy rings in Zanaris are exit rings only:
**There is a fairy ring in the market area that leads to just behind [[Al Kharid]] bank.
**The northern fairy ring leads back to [[Lumbridge Swamp]]s.

===Bank and shop===
There is a [[Zanaris bank|bank]] in Zanaris, close to a [[general store]].

===Market area===
[[File:Zanaris market entrance.png|thumb|The magic doors to the market.]]
The market area lies to the east of Zanaris and costs one [[diamond|cut diamond]] to get in. The gatekeeper will stop players with any sacks from entering.

Here, players can buy [[dragon dagger]]s for 30,000 coins, and [[dragon longsword]]s for 100,000 coins, from [[Jukat]]. Players must have completed the [[Lost City]] quest to be able to wield these powerful weapons.

There is also a [[Irksol_(shop)|jewellery shop]] here that sells [[ruby ring]]s starting from 1,012 coins each, which may be enchanted into [[rings of forging]], useful for [[Smithing|smiths]] with a large amount of iron to be smelted.

There are also two yew trees for [[Woodcutting|woodcutters]], and [[Lunderwin]], who will pay 100 coins for cabbages.

Finally, the exit from the market is to the north-east of the market area; by entering the fairy ring, players will find themselves behind [[Al Kharid]]'s bank. Players cannot return back.

===Cosmic Altar===
The [[Cosmic Altar]] lies to the south of Zanaris. There are two [[Shortcuts|Agility shortcuts]] that allow faster access, requiring 46 Agility for the medium shortcut and 66 Agility for the advanced shortcut. Players will take 4 damage if they fail these shortcuts.

===Crafting===
Near the wheat field inside the city are several [[cow]]s that are reasonably close to the [[bank]].

There is also a [[sand pit]], which is used in glassblowing. If you already have [[soda ash]], the [[furnace]] to the north may be useful for making [[molten glass]] at the same time as collecting [[sand]].

===Cooking===
There is a wheat field and a nearby windmill, so flour is easy to make here. There are also several fountains for collection of [[water]], though these are by no means the closest water-sources to a bank in the game. There is also a [[cooking range]] to the south of the bank.

Among the [[cows]] near the wheat field is a milk cow, and in the windmill, there is a churn. Combine that with the [[bucket]] spawn near the windmill and the nearby bank, and all the requirements for making [[butter]], [[cream]] and [[cheese]] are present.

===Slayer===
[[File:Zanaris throne room.png|thumb|The [[Fairy Mafia]] and the Slayer master.]]
[[Chaeldar]] is the fourth highest level [[Slayer Master]], and requires a minimum [[combat level]] of 70 to take tasks from.

===Evil Chicken's Lair===
{{Main|Evil Chicken's Lair}}
By using a [[raw chicken]] with the shrine of the [[Evil Chicken]] near the entrance from [[Lumbridge Swamp]], players gain access to the [[Evil Chicken's Lair]] with 4 [[black dragon]]s and a [[baby black dragon]] as well.

Mining rocks are also available. Using a rope on the tunnel entrance leads to a small chamber with dragon eggs and the baby black dragon.

===Other features===
[[File:The Blood Moon Rises - The Blood Moon Rises.png|right|thumb|300px|Zanaris seen as a blood moon over [[Morytania]] during [[The Blood Moon Rises]].]]
*There is a [[yew tree]] to the north-east of the bank.
*There is a [[furnace]], but its distance from the bank makes it of little use for anything except possibly glass-making, making use of the nearby [[sand pit]].
*Near the [[Cosmic Altar]], players can gain access to [[Tanglefoot]] creatures seen in the [[Fairytale I - Growing Pains|Fairytale Part I]] quest, as well as [[Mutated Zygomite]]s.
*When players are in Zanaris, they'll often notice strange things happening. Sometimes, a frog or a small [[Zanaris choir|choir]] will come to annoy them, rain clouds can appear over their head or they'll get a sudden urge to dance.
*Players may also be turned into a chicken, pig, or rabbit for a second.
*In the middle of the wheat field is a permanent crop circle to the [[Impetuous Impulses]] minigame.

==Residents==
*[[Fairy Queen]] - The benevolent ruler of Zanaris
*[[Fairy Godfather]] - An evil fairy wishing possession of the Fairy Realm
*[[Slim Louie]] - A henchman of the [[Fairy Godfather]]
*[[Fat Rocco]] - A henchman of the Fairy Godfather
*[[Fairy Nuff]] - A fairy nurse
*[[Fairy Aeryka]] - Tells players of [[Puro-Puro]] and a bit about [[implings]]
*[[Co-ordinator]] - Helps in sending the proper fairies on their way
*[[Fairy Fixit]] - The repairman and creator of the [[fairy ring]]s
*[[Fairy chef]] - A fairy chef
*[[Fairy shop keeper]] - Owns [[Zanaris General Store]]
*[[Fairy shop assistant]] - Helps the shop keeper
*[[Gatekeeper]] - A tree-like figure that guards the gates to and from the marketplace
*[[Jukat]] - Shopkeeper
*[[Irksol]] - Shopkeeper
*[[Lunderwin]] - Shopkeeper
*[[Chaeldar]] - [[Slayer Master]] in Zanaris
*[[Blaec]] - Owner of a [[sand pit]]
*[[Wandering impling]] - Introduces players to the [[Impetuous Impulses]] minigame

===Monsters===
*[[Otherworldly being]]s
*[[Tanglefoot]]
*[[Cow]]s
*[[Zygomite]]s

==Trivia==
[[File:Zanaris Evil Chicken Lair.png|thumb|right|The lower level of the Evil Chicken's Lair as seen from southern Zanaris.]]
*Using the [[Official Client]]'s expanded draw distance, it is possible to see the lower level of the [[Evil Chicken's Lair]] from the southern edge of Zanaris. This is because Zanaris, like all areas not on the overworld map, is actually located on a section of the world map north of the [[Wilderness]] which houses all of the underground and other non-surface areas of the game.
*The [[Zanaris choir]] will follow players into random events.
*Although Zanaris is Gielinor's moon, the city itself is heavily implied to be located somewhere underground, beneath the surface of the moon.{{CiteNPC|npc=Fairy Queen|quote=Clearly you come from a plane dependent on sunlight. Down here, the plants grow in the aura of faerie.|loc=|notes=|name=}}{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/964574157395591168|date=16 February 2018|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/99496|archivedate=29 May 2020|quote=The fairy queen has a line about there not being sunlight "down here", so it does sound like it's a cave in whatever realm it's in.}} The 23 January 2002 update of the game refers to a "zanaris underground city", further reinforcing this theory.

The [[Dungeons|dungeon]] can be accessed during and after the completion of the [[Waterfall Quest]], and is an important destination in the quest. {| |{{Map|2512,3464|r=4|mtype=square|width=250|height=250|caption=The entrance to the dungeon.|stroke=#ffff00|fill=#ffff00}} |} ==Transportation== '''Note: Players must use a [[rope]] to reach the dungeon's entrance unless they have completed the [[medium Kandarin Diary]]. Players who have not completed Waterfall Quest must also have [[Glarial's amulet]] in their [[inventory]] (or be wearing it) to gain entry to the dungeon - it is not needed after the quest.''' A quick way of getting to [[Baxtorian Falls]] is using a [[Games necklace|games necklace]] and travelling to [[Barbarian Outpost]], then running south. When you have both of these items, go to the house above the Baxtorian Falls. West of it, behind a gate, there is a [[Log raft (Waterfall Dungeon)|log raft]]. Click the raft to ride it and you will crash into a little island. '''Do not''' use the available left-click option to swim to the rock to the south; instead, '''use your [[rope]] on that rock'''. Once you have safely reached the rock, you are at the top of the Baxtorian Falls. Again, '''do not''' fall for the left-click option on the dead tree, but '''use your rope on that tree''' to climb down. You now will be on a small ledge with a barrel and an entrance. If you have completed [[Waterfall Quest]] or have [[Glarial's amulet]] with you, you may safely enter the dungeon. Otherwise, the barrel allows you to leave the ledge without losing [[Hitpoints]]. If you try to enter without the amulet, or if you forgot to use the rope instead of either of the left-click options, you will fall down the waterfall and wash up to the south, ''losing 8 Hitpoints''. You will then have to run back north onto the top of the waterfall and start over. ==Features== {{Map:Waterfall Dungeon}} Within the [[Dungeons|dungeon]], [[aggressive]] [[monsters]] range from level 16-86, with the higher-levelled [[fire giant]]s reaching a max hit of 11. The dungeon is popular among [[Ironmen]], due to the much sought after [[rune scimitar]] drop from the fire giants. It is also a possible location to be assigned to kill fire giants from [[Konar quo Maten|Konar]] as a [[Slayer]] task. The dungeon consists of six different areas:
# A cavern with five [[shadow spider]]s. # A room with crates with [[A key (Waterfall Dungeon)|a key]], needed for three [[quests]]. # A room with seven [[fire giant]]s. # A room with four fire giants. Three shadow spiders can wander into this room if the door is left open. # The path to the [[Chalice of Eternity]]. # A room with the [[Chalice of Eternity]].
{{Clear|left}} ==Safespots== The Waterfall Dungeon is often used to kill [[fire giant]]s. There are [[safespot]]s in the dungeon, commonly used by low-mid levels for training [[Ranged]] and [[Magic]], though [[halberd]]s can also be used for [[Melee]] training. File:Fire giant (Waterfall Dungeon, 1) safespot.png|A safespot in the western room of the Dungeon, after the fire giants become [[unaggressive]]. File:Fire giant (Waterfall Dungeon, 2) safespot.png|A safespot in the middle room of the dungeon, after the fire giants become unaggressive. File:Fire giant (Waterfall Dungeon, 3) safespot.png|A safespot on the western room next to the northern door. File:Fire giant (Waterfall Dungeon, 4) safespot.png|A safespot on the eastern tile next to the inner doors of the middle room of the dungeon. Cannons may be used in the Waterfall Dungeon, although it is a single way combat zone. ==Monsters== There are four different monsters in this dungeon: *[[Shadow spider]]s, combat level 52, drain [[Prayer]] and are invisible on the [[minimap]] *[[Skeleton]]s, combat level 45 *[[Skeleton Mage]]s, combat level 16 *[[Fire giant]]s, combat level 86, max hit of 11 ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 20 May 2026 |update = The Red Reef is Out Today! |change = You can once again access the Waterfall Dungeon without a rope, provided you meet the requirements. }} {{Subject changes |date = 17 September 2025 |update = Poll 85 - Bridges, Boots, Ropes & Roots |poll = Poll 85 - Clan Chat and Player Tweaks |change = After completion of [[Waterfall Quest]] and the [[medium Kandarin Diary]], players no longer need to bring a [[rope]] to use on the rock and dead tree in order to access the dungeon. }} {{Subject changes |date = 16 March 2017 |update = Quality of Life & Deadman Prep |poll = Quality of Life - General Suggestions |change = Players can now enter the Waterfall dungeon without [[Glarial's Amulet]] if they have completed the [[Waterfall Quest]]. }} {{Subject changes |date = 10 May 2004 |update = Dueling changes |change = Increased the quantity of fire giant spawns in the Waterfall Dungeon. }} {{Subject changes footer}} {{Waterfall Dungeon}} {{Roving Elves}} {{Waterfall Quest}} {{Dungeons}} [[Category:Quest locations]] [[Category:Kandarin]]

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Location |name = Keldagrim |image = [[File:Keldagrim.png|300px]] |release = [[31 May]] [[2005]] |update = Keldagrim - The Dwarven City |members = Yes |location = [[Dwarven Realm]] |race = [[Dwarf (race)|Dwarves]] |teleport = [[Minigame Teleport]] ([[Blast Furnace]]), [[Dorgesh-Kaan]] ([[Dorgesh-Kaan–Keldagrim train system|Train]]) |music = [[Tale of Keldagrim]], [[Land of the Dwarves]] |map = {{Map|name=Keldagrim|x=2879|y=10176|zoom=1|mapID=10}} |type = settlement |leagueRegion = Fremennik }} {{Relative location |name = Keldagrim |north = Trollweiss and Rellekka Hunter area |south = Seers' Village |east = Mountain Camp |west = Rellekka }} '''Keldagrim''' is the city of the [[dwarves]]. Its name is derived from the [[River Kelda]] flowing through the city, and it is a massive underground settlement accessible from the tunnel entrance east of [[Rellekka]]. It is first visited during [[The Giant Dwarf]] quest. This is also the home of the [[Blast Furnace]] and the [[Rat Pits]]. After the completion of [[Another Slice of H.A.M.|Another Slice of H.A.M]], players can use the [[Dorgesh-Kaan–Keldagrim train system]] to travel between the city of [[Dorgesh-Kaan]] and Keldagrim. The city is divided into two parts by the river: the rich Keldagrim-West and the poorer Keldagrim-East. The [[Keldagrim Palace]] sits in the centre of the city, accessible from both halves. The city was once a monarchy during the so-called Age of Kings, but is currently ruled by a [[Consortium]] of the eight most powerful trading companies. ==History== Keldagrim was founded millennia ago by a lost clan of magic-using dwarves who'd gone underground to escape the [[God Wars]] on the surface.{{CiteNPC |npc=Postie Pete|quote=Did you know that Keldagrim was originally constructed by a long lost clan who embraced the power of magic, and used it to aid with glorious buildings like the royal palace? They even stayed down there for 1000 years or more, in a time they call 'The age of Kings'.|name=postie}}{{CiteNPC |npc=Rind the gardener |loc=The Giant Dwarf |quote=We dwarves went underground a long time ago, see. For a while the city of Keldagrim was completely cut off from the rest of Gielinor simply waiting out the wars of the humans and the gods.}}{{NamedRef|hugi}} At some point, the dwarves lost their ability to (or otherwise stopped using) magic, instead focusing on developing technology instead. The history of Keldagrim is thereafter divided into at least three periods, most of which take place in the [[Fourth Age]]. They include the Era of Kings, the Rise of the Consortium, and the Era of Prosperity, as these eras are supposedly documented in the [[Keldagrim Library]].{{CiteNPC |npc=Librarian|loc=The Giant Dwarf|quote='''Librarian:''' You'll find books dating from many different eras as well, such as the Era of Kings, the Rise of the Consortium and the Era of Prosperity, our current era.
'''Player:''' How do these eras correspond with the Ages of the world?
'''Librarian:''' Oh, they are quite different, and most of them take place in the Fourth Age. Since dwarves hid underground for a long time to sit out the wars that rages above the ground our history books differ slightly from those written by humans|name=hugi}} The Era of Kings (also known as the Age of Kings), when Keldagrim was ruled by a monarch, began at some point after the city's founding and lasted over 1000 years.{{NamedRef|postie}} Steam power was not fully developed by the dwarves at this time, so it was very difficult for them to acquire enough food to feed the city. {{CiteNPC |npc= Rind the gardener|loc=The Giant Dwarf |quote=In the Era of Kings, many centuries ago, it was harder of course. Our steam technology was not developed as far yet and getting fresh supplies of food was always a problem.}} Accordingly, this era is referred to as "the dark days".{{CiteText |text=The Giant Dwarf|quote=Five hundred years have passed since the rule of King Alvis, saviour of Keldagrim, victim of his own intentions. He founded the Consortium: the gathering of mining companies that were to serve the monarchy. But eventually the monarchy came to serve the Consortium. By the time of his death, the monarchy was all but abolished.Now the Kings in Keldagrim are but a distant memory, with only the statue of King Alvis to remind the people of the old days. The dark days.|notes=(opening cutscene)|name=cutscene}} The dwarves had no contact with the surface until the reign of [[King Alvis]]. After his victory against a troll invasion, the dwarves cautiously reestablished contact.{{CiteNPC |npc=Rind the gardener|loc=The Giant Dwarf|quote=Only when King Alvis heroically defended the city against an invasion of trolls did we dare to venture out and see how much the world had changed.}} Their relationship to humans was initially hostile. Humans dared not even go underground for fear of dwarven aggression.{{CiteNPC |npc=Wise Old Man|quote=Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.}} The Rise of the Consortium was marked by the end of King Alvis' reign roughly 500 years ago. The king founded the Consortium, an assembly of the city's mining companies, to aid the monarchy, but it ended up supplanting it entirely. By the king's death, the monarchy was effectively abolished.{{NamedRef|cutscene}} At some point later, The Era of Prosperity began, which is the current period.{{NamedRef|hugi}} After the Consortium came to power, the steam engine was developed over the next centuries.{{CiteNPC |npc=Cart Conductor|loc=The Giant Dwarf|quote=Oh, no no, we dwarves don't use magic. All of this is powered by steam engines, developed over the past few centuries after the Consortium came to power.}} Keldagrim cannot produce most of its food by itself, so the steam-powered minecart network is instrumental in ensuring the city is properly fed.{{CiteNPC |npc=Rind the gardener|loc=The Giant Dwarf|quote=We can grow a little food underground, but most of it comes from the extensive steamcart network that runs beneath the earth.}} ==Transportation== Travelling to Keldagrim requires starting [[The Giant Dwarf]] quest. The quest can be started by talking to the [[dwarven boatman]] just outside the city, in the cave north-east of [[Rellekka]]. [[File:Getting to Keldagrim.png|thumb|A few methods of getting to Keldagrim.]] * A common method of getting to Keldagrim is by using the [[Trapdoor (Grand Exchange)|trapdoor]] located in the north-west of the [[Grand Exchange]] to take a [[Keldagrim mine cart system|minecart]] to the south-eastern section of the city. ** Additionally, Keldagrim can be travelled to via minecart from the underground [[White Wolf Mountain]] passageway or the [[Dwarven Mine]] under [[Ice Mountain]] for a fee of 100 or 150 [[coins]] respectively. * Players can use [[fairy ring]] code {{Fairycode|dks}} to teleport right next to the cave entrance to Keldagrim. * Players can also use an [[enchanted lyre]] or [[Fremennik sea boots]], and then walk north-east around the outside of Rellekka to reach the entrance to Keldagrim. * After completing [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]], players can use the [[Dorgesh-Kaan–Keldagrim train system]]. * Players can also use the [[Minigame Teleport]] for either the [[Blast Furnace]] or the [[Rat Pits]] (requiring [[Ratcatchers]] to be completed). * After completion of the quest [[Between a Rock...]], players can use a [[ring of wealth]] to teleport to [[Dondakan]]'s rock which gets players close to the ferry system that can be used to enter Keldagrim. '''It should be noted that 2 coins will be needed in order to cross the river to travel via the dwarven boatman.''' ==Quests== *[[The Giant Dwarf]] may be started by speaking to the [[Dwarven Boatman]] inside the dungeon east of [[Rellekka]]. (You need to start this quest to gain access to Keldagrim) *[[Between a Rock...]] may be started by speaking to [[Dondakan]] in the south-west corner of Keldagrim. *[[Forgettable Tale of a Drunken Dwarf]] may be started by speaking to [[Veldaban]] west of the bank in Keldagrim. ==Bank== {{Main|Keldagrim bank}} ==Shops== [[File:Keldagrim east.png|thumb|The poorer Keldagrim East.]] Keldagrim plays host to more shops than any other city in Gielinor. As such, the city is a major attraction for those wishing to buy things. It hosts a wide range of [[shop]]s, and is well-known for its vast assortment of available goods. ===Gunslik's Assorted Items=== [[Gunslik's Assorted Items]] is on the western side of Keldagrim. It's a [[general store]] run by [[Gunslik]], selling supplies that should come in handy during adventuring. Its stock is somewhat similar to the general stores in [[Karamja]]. ===Pickaxe-Is-Mine=== [[Pickaxe-Is-Mine]] is on the eastern side of Keldagrim. It's a [[mining shop]] that's run by [[Tati]] and [[Sune]], which sells every type of pickaxe with the exception of [[Iron pickaxe|iron]], [[Black pickaxe|black]] and [[Dragon pickaxe|dragon]]. This store is very convenient for [[ironman mode|ironmen]] because it allows players to purchase newer, more effective pickaxes while training mining in the city. ===Keldagrim Stonemason=== [[Keldagrim Stonemason]] is on the western side of Keldagrim. Run by the [[Stonemason]], it is one of the only two masonry stores currently in the game. The store sells mid-to-high-level construction materials, ranging from basic [[limestone brick]] to [[gold leaf]] and [[magic stone]]s. ===Quality Armour Shop=== [[Quality Armour Shop]] is on the western side of Keldagrim. The shop is run by [[Saro]] and sells a variety of [[melee armour]] and [[shield]]s. There is also an anvil in the shop players can use. ===Quality Weapons Shop=== [[Quality Weapons Shop]] is on the western side of Keldagrim. The shop is run by [[Santiri]] and sells various [[Weapons#Weapon_requirements|melee weapons]] and also [[Weapons#Ranged_weapons|ranged weapons]]. ===Agmundi Quality Clothes=== [[Agmundi Quality Clothes]] is on the western side of Keldagrim. It's a [[Clothes shops|clothes shop]] run by [[Agmundi]] and gets most of her stock from [[Vermundi]] (her sister). As such, she is the first destination for dwarves in need of new clothing. The clothing sold here is much too small for humans to comfortably wear, although some players wear it anyway. ===Vermundi's Clothes Stall=== [[Vermundi's Clothes Stall]] is on the eastern side of Keldagrim. It's a [[Clothes shops|clothes shop]] run by [[Vermundi]]. Most of her merchandise is sent to Agmundi (her sister) so the stock here is somewhat lacking. Although this stall has a thieve option, it cannot actually be stolen from. ===Vigr's Warhammers=== [[Vigr's Warhammers]] is on the western side of Keldagrim. The '''Lighthouse''' is an area north of the [[Barbarian Outpost]], and features prominently in the [[Horror from the Deep]] quest. The Lighthouse can only be entered during and after the quest; however, the island itself can be visited prior to starting the quest. [[Jossik]] can be found upstairs after completing the aforementioned quest. He runs a [[general store]] and will provide players with [[god book]]s, as well as replace any that are lost.

Its dungeon is a popular place for players to kill [[dagannoth]] for [[Slayer]]. 

==Transportation==
The fastest way getting there is [[fairy ring]] code {{Fairycode|alp}}. Players can get there from the [[Barbarian Outpost]] by jumping across the northern [[basalt rock]]s that protrude from the sea. It is possible to slip on the rocks, which results in the player falling into the water, being swept back to shore, and taking up to 10 damage. It is noted that having an [[Agility]] level above 35 increases the likelihood of successfully jumping across the rocks. Players seem to have a lot of trouble getting over the rock as the character "fails" to jump over it several times.

Another route of access is via a bridge, which is fixed during the quest. The bridge is located in the south-western part of the [[Fremennik Province]]. If the bridge has not been fixed, the player can jump across it and gain 1 Agility experience, but failing to cross the bridge will deal anywhere between 1 and 5 damage and grant 0.7 Agility experience.

Besides the fairy ring, there are three teleports that arrive near the Lighthouse:
*A [[games necklace]] or [[Minigame Teleport]] to the Barbarian Outpost.
*[[Teleport to House]], if the player's house is at [[Rellekka]].
*An [[enchanted lyre]] teleport to the entrance to Rellekka.

==Features==
[[File:Lighthouse floors.png|thumb|Maps of the Lighthouse]]
The Lighthouse is the start point of the quest [[Horror from the Deep]], and is where most of the quest takes place. It cannot be entered until [[Larrissa]], who stands outside the Lighthouse, gives the player the [[Lighthouse key]]. After unlocking the door for the first time, the key is no longer needed.

===Ground floor===
The {{FloorNumber|uk=0}} has the stairs to the {{FloorNumber|uk=1}} and a metal ladder to the basement.

===First floor===
The {{FloorNumber|uk=1}} is the room for the Lighthouse's tender. It contains a bed, bookcase, two sets of drawers, and stairs leading up and down.

[[Jossik]] can be found here after the player rescues him in the quest. He replaces [[Silas]] as the keeper of the Lighthouse. Jossik runs a [[general store]] in this room. Besides the usual items like [[hammer]]s and [[rope]], the store also sells:
*[[Poison (item)|Poison]]. This is '''not''' [[weapon poison]]. Instead, it is a poison that is used in some quests, such as [[Ernest the Chicken]].
*[[Pestle and mortar]]s and [[vial]]s, both of which are used mostly for [[Herblore]].
*A large variety of alcoholic beverages: [[brandy]], [[dwarven stout]], [[gin]], [[Greenman's ale]], [[grog]], [[vodka]], [[whiskey]], and [[Wizard's mind bomb]].

Jossik will replace a player's [[damaged book]] or [[god book]] if it is lost, with collected pages intact. He will also sell a new book for 5,000 coins.

===Second floor===
The {{FloorNumber|uk=2}} contains the light and its mechanism. The player repairs the mechanism during the [[Horror from the Deep]] quest.

The Lighthouse building is difficult to see from the ground, but a better view of it is possible on this floor.

===Basement===
The basement contains the ladder back up, a small pool of water, and a door to the north. Beyond the door is a foyer with a ladder down into the dungeon.

At first, the door is a [[strange wall (Lighthouse)|strange wall]], which the player activates during the quest. Once activated, the wall becomes two one-way doorways. The eastern door is used to enter the foyer from the basement and the western one is used to enter the basement from the foyer.

After the quest, you can re-enter the dungeon by clicking on the piece of blank wall beside the door ("open wall"), since clicking on the door itself will only show a puzzle.

===Dungeon===
[[File:Lighthouse Dungeon.png|thumb|300px|left|The Dagannoth caverns beneath the Lighthouse.]]
The dungeon is a single large chamber. The westernmost part is a pool of water, presumably connecting to the sea outside, while the rest is dry land. The dungeon also connects to the [[Waterbirth Island Dungeon]], which has a one-way exit into the Lighthouse Dungeon.

After the quest, the dungeon is crawling with many [[dagannoth]]. It is a [[multi-combat area]], and the dagannoth here, although moderately strong, are inaccurate in their attacks and are not as powerful as their levels suggest. The lower level dagannoth shoot spikes at players as a rather poor [[Ranged]] attack, and the higher level dagannoth attack with a slightly more accurate close-range ([[Melee]]) bite. Many dagannoth wander about near the entrance ladder, so players should be prepared for combat as soon as they descend into the dungeon.

The '''Brine Rat Cavern''', also known as '''Sven's cave''', is a dungeon accessible during and after [[Olaf's Quest]]. Players can enter the dungeon by digging with a [[spade]] south of the [[windswept tree]], which is on a plateau east of [[Olaf Hradson]] and south-east of the [[Rellekka Hunter area]]. When the hole is dug, the player falls through it and is stunned for a few seconds, but no damage is taken.

The south-western part of the cavern contains the exit back to the surface world. To exit, the player must roll back the rock to expose a cave leading to the outside. After exiting, the rock rolls back to block the cave, so the cavern cannot be entered by this route.

The cavern actually consists of the main cavern, an outdoors area on the coast, a slippery walkway, another outdoors, coastal area, and a small shallow cavern south of the second coastal area. Neither of the coastal areas appear on the [[world map]], so the entire complex is considered a single [[List of dungeons|dungeon]].

The entire cavern is a single combat zone. [[Dwarf multicannons]] may be used here.

==Transportation==
The Brine Rat Cavern is in the north-eastern region of the [[Fremennik Province]], and requires a [[spade]] to access. This is a remote area and takes some time to walk to. There are some faster means to get here:

*[[Fairy ring]] code {{Fairycode|DKS}} is very close to the cavern's entrance. Use of the fairy rings requires players to complete at least part of the [[Fairytale II - Cure a Queen]] quest.
*The [[Eagle transport system]] flies to the [[Rellekka Hunter area]], which is north of the dungeon's entrance. Players must have completed the [[Eagles' Peak]] quest to use an eagle to fly here.
*The passage to [[Keldagrim]] is close to the cavern's entrance. Players must have at least started [[The Giant Dwarf]] quest to have access to Keldagrim. Keldagrim is important in that two transport systems go there:
**The [[Keldagrim minecart system|mine cart]]s run to Keldagrim from three locations. One is the tunnel under [[White Wolf Mountain]]; access to the tunnel requires completion of the [[Fishing Contest]] quest. The second location is in the [[Dwarven Mine]] under [[Ice Mountain]]. The third is a hatch in the north-west part of [[Grand Exchange]]. All carts are free of charge.
**A [[Dorgesh-Kaan–Keldagrim train system|train system]] runs between [[Dorgesh-Kaan]] and Keldagrim. The train is free to use but requires the player to have completed [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]] quest.
*The [[slayer ring]] teleport to the [[Fremennik Slayer Dungeon]] is just south of the Brine Rat cavern.
*The use of an [[enchanted lyre]] will teleport the player outside the gates of [[Rellekka]], just south of the cavern entrance.

==Features==

The cavern has the following features:

:1. Entrance from the outside world. You cannot return to the surface here.

:2. Exit to the outside world. There is a cave passage behind a rock here. You exit the cavern by rolling the rock out of the way and then using the passage.

:3. [[Giant bat]]s

:4. [[Brine rat]]s - These rats are not aggressive and have some good drops, including many [[death rune]]s, noted raw [[shark]]s, noted raw [[lobster]]s, the rare [[Brine sabre]], and other items. 

:5. [[Skeleton fremennik]]s - These are level 40. [[Skeleton]]s here or in Area 7 can be killed to obtain a [[Key (Olaf's Quest)|key to the gate]].

:6. Picture door. During [[Olaf's Quest]], players must solve a picture puzzle to open this door. Afterwards, players can open the door using a right-click option.

:7. First coastal area. This is outdoors but does not appear on the world map. Skeleton fremenniks, levels 50 and 60, are here, as is one [[Rock Crab]]. Skeletons here or in Area 5 can be killed to obtain a key to the gate. Players can collect [[rope]] and [[Rotten barrel|rotting barrels]] here. (A player can quickly collect a full inventory of rope, but the area's distance from a bank makes it inconvenient as a free rope source for most purposes.)

:8. [[Olaf's_Quest#The_rotten_walkway|Slippery wooden walkway]]. This connects the two coastal areas. A good [[Agility]] level helps in crossing the walkway. Possibly, walking (not running) one square at a time across the walkway may help. If you slip, you will fall into the sea and be washed up on shore in the outside world, near the exit point of the cavern. The walkway does '''not''' become safer after the quest.
[[File:Sven's shipwreck.png|thumb|The remains of Sven's ship and Ulfric's grave.]]
:9. Gate - When travelling west-to-east, this gate must be unlocked with a key dropped by a Skeleton fremennik you kill. Clicking on the gate calls a puzzle screen where you must match the shape of the key to correct lock. The key can have five different shapes. Unlike the picture door, even after the quest you must solve this puzzle each time you want to open the gate from the west. The key disappears when you unlock the gate. You do not need a key to open the gate when travelling in the other direction (east-to-west).

:10. Second coastal area. This has level 60 Skeleton fremenniks and another rock crab. The wreck of [[Ulfric]]'s ship is here, as is Ulfric's gravestone marking his grave. During [[Olaf's Quest]], a chest is also here, and opening it triggers the climactic battle between you and Ulfric's skeleton. The back (south) of this coastal area turns into a small, shallow cavern.

==Uses==

*[[Brine rat]] is the only source for the rare drop [[Brine sabre]],  a stronger alternative to the [[Rune scimitar]] that can also be used for finishing off [[Rockslug|rockslugs]] without the use of a [[bag of salt]].

'''Fossil Island''' is a [[members]]-only area located north-east of [[Morytania]] and unveils a unique environment where players can train a variety of skills. It is an ancient, uncharted island currently being explored by the [[Varrock Museum]].

The island itself is surrounded by seven other smaller islands, though they are currently inaccessible save for [[Lithkren]], the island north-west that players visit during the quest [[Dragon Slayer II]].

In order to reach the island, players must have completed the [[Bone Voyage]] [[Quests|quest]].

Fossil Island uses a form of currency called [[Numulite]].

==Transportation==
Initially, Fossil Island could only be reached via the [[Canal barge|barge]] from the [[Digsite]], which is close to the [[Varrock Teleport]].

===Digsite pendant===
The fastest way to travel to Fossil Island is to use a [[digsite pendant]], which will teleport the player near the barge at the Digsite, where they can fast travel to the [[Museum Camp]] by speaking to the [[barge guard]]. 
[[File:Magic_Mushtree_map.png|thumb|200px|A map showing the locations of the magic mushtrees.]]
The pendant can be used on the southernmost [[Strange Machine|strange machine]] inside the [[House on the Hill]], north-east of the Museum Camp, to unlock the 'Fossil Island' (or house) teleport option. There is also a [[Mycelium Transportation System|magic mushtree]] at the house that utilises the [[Mycelium Transportation System]]; this system of magic mushtrees allows transportation around Fossil Island, but in order to access them, they must be discovered by walking to their locations first and attempting to use them.

===Alternate===
If a digsite pendant is not available, several other options to reach the [[Digsite]] are available.

The fastest way is to use a [[Digsite teleport scroll]] which teleports players south-west of the barge.

Alternatively, [[gnome glider]] transport to Lemanto Andra, the glider landing site south-west of the barge, can be suitable with easy access to a glider. Players can use a [[ring of dueling]] to teleport to the [[Emir's Arena]] to use the glider west of the gem trader in [[Al Kharid]], the [[Cowbell amulet]] and run south east to the glider west of the gem trader in [[Al Kharid]], or travel to the [[Gnome Stronghold]] via a [[royal seed pod]] after completion of [[Monkey Madness II]] to use the glider atop the [[Grand Tree]].

==Areas==
===Museum Camp===
{{Main|Museum Camp}}
[[File:Museum Camp.png|thumb|250px|The Museum Camp.]]
After arriving on Fossil Island, the player will be just west of the [[Museum Camp]]. At first, the camp will not be very useful, but players can utilise their [[Construction]] skill and materials to build improvements within the camp. A list of these, along with other activities on the island, can be found on a [[Notice_board_(Museum_Camp)#Museum_Camp|notice board]] at the camp's western edge.

To build the bank, players will need a [[hammer]], 21 [[Construction]], 2 [[oak plank|oak planks]], 1 [[iron bar]], and 5 [[nails]]. See the [[Museum Camp|camp's page]] for a list of other constructable utilities and their required materials. You will need 29 [[Construction]] to build everything. 

There is a [[Fossil Storage|fossil storage]] crate East of the camp which can store [[Fossil Island fossil|fossils]] found whilst on the island. There are additional crates scattered elsewhere around the island, and one in the [[Varrock Museum]] basement.

===Mushroom Forest===
{{Main|Mushroom Forest}}
[[File:Mushroom Forest.png|thumb|left|250px|The Mushroom Forest.]]
The north-west section of the island is the [[Mushroom Forest]]. There are various activities here that allow players to train a variety of [[skills]]. Players can slay [[Ancient Zygomite|ancient zygomites]] as part of a [[zygomite]] [[Slayer task]], track down [[herbiboar]]s throughout the forest, plant [[hardwood tree]]s in the three [[Farming/Patch locations#Special tree patches|tree patches]] in the south-east corner, and calcify fossils in the [[mycelium pool]].

In addition, the [[Wyvern Cave]] can be found in the Mushroom Forest beneath a trapdoor. The [[wyverns]] within can only be slain if players have been assigned Fossil Island wyverns as a Slayer task.

===Tar Swamp===
{{Main|Tar Swamp}}
[[File:Tar Swamp.png|thumb|250px|The Tar Swamp.]]
The south-west section of the island contains a large swamp. Travelling through the swamp requires a [[rake]] to clear vines in addition to an [[axe]] to chop down thick vines. [[Sulliuscep]] mushrooms can be found throughout the swamp, but only one can be chopped down, forcing players to traverse the hostile swamp while avoiding aggressive [[Tar Monster|tar monsters]] to find the choppable sulliuscep. There is also a [[rubber cap mushroom]] that can be used to launch the player next to a Magic Mushtree, but this can inflict up to 50+ damage if the player has not filled the landing pit with [[Mushroom|mushrooms]].

In the southern end of the swamp, players will find the [[deranged archaeologist]], who fights similarly to the [[crazy archaeologist]] found in the [[Wilderness]] [[Ruins (west)|ruins]]. However, he is much more dangerous, as his [[special attack]] can hit for 56 damage.

===Volcano===
{{Main|Fossil Island Volcano}}

The volcano can be found on the south-east side of the island. Many [[ash pile]]s can be found here, along with the [[Volcanic Mine]].

===Bank chest island===
A small island can be found north of Fossil Island, which can be accessed either by using the [[Rowboat (Fossil Island)|rowboat]] at the north-east corner of the [[Mushroom Forest]], or by using the [[Zip line (Fossil Island)|zip line]] on the House on the Hill, which requires 74 [[Agility]]. It contains a [[Bank Chest-wreck|bank chest]].

===Underwater===
{{Main|Underwater}}
[[File:Underwater.png|thumb|250px|left|The underwater area beneath Fossil Island.]]
While on the bank chest island, the player can use the rowboat to dive beneath the waters of Fossil Island.

Unlike other underwater areas throughout the game, a small bar indicating the player's oxygen level will appear at the top left of the game screen when they enter the area. This bar will continually drain while the player remains underwater; if it runs out, players will drown and reappear at the surface. You can refill your oxygen by collecting [[pufferfish]], which can be consumed to refill your oxygen. However, if the player has a [[fishbowl helmet]] and [[diving apparatus]] equipped (or [[medallion of the deep]]), their oxygen level will stay at 100%. The helmet and apparatus can be safely removed and re-equipped while underwater, and if you have an oxygen level below 100%, it will slowly fill back up once both items are re-equipped.

===House on the Hill===
{{Main|House on the Hill}}
[[File:House on the Hill.png|thumb|250px|The House on the Hill, an ancient dragonkin structure.]]
Located on the north-east side of the island, the [[House on the Hill]] can be travelled to by climbing a hill on the south end of the [[Mushroom Forest]]. Within the house are various [[Strange Machine|strange machines]], one of which can enchant a [[digsite pendant]] to allow players to [[Teleportation|teleport]] directly to the house. Additionally, one of the four [[Mycelium Transportation System|magic mushtrees]] on the island can be found here, allowing quick access to other parts of the island by teleporting here via digsite pendant and then using the magic mushtree to travel.
[[File:House_on_the_Hill_basement.png|thumb|left|250px|The house's basement. In the centre lies a strange grid with missing pieces.]]
In the basement of the house, accessible via a trapdoor in the south-east corner, there are several [[Stone chest (House on the Hill)|stone chests]] with a search option. Searching the stone chest will ask for a [[numulite]]. After inserting the numulite, the chest will give the search option to insert 100 numulites into the hole. The chests have a chance of having nothing happen, dealing damage, or giving one of various notes. The notes can be added to the player's [[Fossil island note book|Fossil Island note book]]. In addition, behind the ladder, a pile of books can be searched to obtain an [[ancient diary]].

The '''Myths' Guild''' is a [[guild]] located on the south-western tip of [[Feldip Hills]]. It is accessible only to those who have proved their worth by helping uncover the lost history of the world to fill the guild's [[Library of knowledge|Library of Knowledge]].{{CiteNPC|npc=Alec Kincade|quote=Help us fill our Library of Knowledge. In return, we will grant you access to the guild and you will reap the rewards within.|loc=Dragon Slayer II}} The [[player]] can gain access by helping uncover the lost history of the origin of [[dragon]]s by completing the [[Dragon Slayer II]] [[quest]].

[[Alec Kincade]] is the headmaster of the guild, and he is also the start point of Dragon Slayer II.

==History==
Founded by the [[Sect of Uhld]], the Guild's primary goal is information preservation,{{CiteNPC|npc=Erdan|quote=They [the Sect] quickly established this guild with information preservation as their core goal, for men are recorders of history and magic is key for this to last.}} as well as distinguishing fact and myths throughout history, all of which are archived in the guild's Library of Knowledge.{{CiteNPC|npc=Alec Kincade|quote=As time passes, that which was once fact, becomes myth. Some tales are just that, tales. However, some tales are something more. Here at the Myths' Guild, we live to tell the difference between the two. If you wish to join us, you must do the same.}}

The Guild was founded sometime during the [[Runecrafting Crusades]] in the [[Fifth Age]], after the Sect of Uhld witnessed the destruction of the entrance to the [[Wrath Altar]], which had been discovered after sometime during the southern crusades.{{CiteNPC|npc=Erdan|quote=The story my father told me was of a war on magic. Of god fearing men who believed nothing good would come of wielding a power that was never meant for them. And so the rune temples that man had created were under threat. Before long, all were destroyed and thus forgotten. But the wrath that these Gunnites embraced rippled through the pocket dimensions. Supposedly, a new altar of power was discovered.}} Upon studying the altar, they were able to create [[surge spells]] and destroyed the Gunnites of the southern crusade.{{CiteNPC|npc=Erdan|quote=...the Sect of Uhld had used the information gained from the wrath altar, and with a spell of their own making, they destroyed the southern runecrafting crusade with much ease.}}

*[[Spirit tree]] - to [[Feldip Hills]], just east of the entrance.
*[[Charter ship]] - to [[Corsair Cove]] and run west.

==History==
Long ago, Vampyrium was visited by the [[god]] [[Zaros]], who taught the then tribal vampyres of society and culture, and thus laid foundation to the vampyric society.{{CiteText|text=A taste of hope (book)|author=Lowerniel Drakan|quote= The arrival of the Stranger from Afar brought an end to the tribal system, with him forming the tribes into the early houses of Vampyrium. He introduced to us alien cultural concepts such as society and art.|page=|loc=Sins of the Father|notes=|name=}} With Zaros's teachings, the vampyres eventually became the dominant species of the planet, their organisation and cooperation making them able to outmatch their [[Yarasa]] competitors.

Eight [[Vampyre Houses]] were formed from the tribes, and [[Lowerniel Drakan]], head of the newly formed [[Vampyre Houses#House Drakan|House Drakan]], was quick to gain power, co-opting the neighboring houses by draining their leaders of their blood. House Drakan became the prevailing power on Vampyrium,{{CiteText|text=A taste of hope (book)|author=Lowerniel Drakan|quote=Before the concept of laws were passed on to our newborn aristocracy, I seized an opportunity to co-opt my neighbouring houses by draining their leaders of blood. These smaller houses fell under my leadership, and the House of Drakan became the prevailing power on Vampyrium. |page=|loc=Sins of the Father|notes=|name=}} with most of the others submitting to its rule while rivals that resisted, such as the [[Vampyre Houses#House Alzeph|Alzeph]] and [[Vampyre Houses#House Pyrah|Pyrah]] Houses, were wiped out.{{CiteText|text=A taste of hope (book)|author=Lowerniel Drakan|quote= (...) and the Alzeph now being wiped out.|page=|loc=Sins of the Father|notes=|name=}}{{CiteText|text=A taste of hope (book)|author=Lowerniel Drakan|quote= (...) I had the entire blood stores of the Pyrah destroyed, and the tribe alongside it.|page=|loc=Sins of the Father|notes=|name=}}

In the [[Second Age]] of [[Gielinor]], [[Zaros]] once more returned to Vampyrium and requested the [[vampyres]] to join him and contribute to the [[Zarosian Empire]]. Many vampyres left the world to join Zaros, including the most prominent leaders of the various Vampyre Houses.{{CiteText|text=Arachnids of Vampyrium|author=|quote=When the Stranger from Afar led the vampyres to Gielinor...|page=|loc=Theatre of Blood}} Any remaining vampyres on the planet were likely killed by the numerous predators or reverted into a feral state, except for one - [[Sugadinti Vitur]], who was assisted by his numerous [[aranei]] followers.

Millennia later, Lord Drakan, who had since rebelled against Zaros, conquered [[Hallowvale]] and waged numerous wars against other kingdoms, returned to Vampyrium, utilising [[Efaritay Hallow]]'s blood.{{NamedRef|wildHunt}} He hunted down [[Xarpus]], the King and last of the [[yarasa]], which he brought back to [[Gielinor]] to be used as a beast in the [[Theatre of Blood]]. When Efaritay escaped and he ran out of her blood, he was no longer able to return to Vampyrium until [[Safalaan Hallow]] was captured during [[Sins of the Father]].

The '''Meiyerditch Laboratories''' are a set of winding tunnels beneath the [[Sanguinesti Region]] where the vampyres practised [[haemalchemy]] until they were suddenly shut down by [[Lord Drakan]]. Various gruesome experiments were conducted there on humans and bloodveld. The northern end of the tunnels connects to [[Myreque Hideout|the tomb]] of [[Ivandis Seergaze]].

During the quest [[Darkness of Hallowvale]], the player visits the laboratories in search of possible research that may aid [[The Myreque]] in their fight against the vampyres, and during [[Sins of the Father]], the player and [[Safalaan]] visits further beyond for additional research.

Access to the complete laboratory is granted after the player kills the [[mutated bloodveld]] that appears during the [[Sins of the Father]] quest, though players are recommended to complete the quest until acquiring [[Vyre noble clothing]] for easier laboratory access.

In the southern part of the dungeon, near the mutated bloodvelds, there are 3 [[log]] respawns and [[tinderbox]]. In the eastern part, [[crawling hand]]s can be found as well. The entire area is also [[multicombat]] and the [[Dwarven multicannon]] '''can''' be used here thus making it an excellent place to kill bloodvelds with a cannon.

The entrance to the true [[Blood Altar]] is located within the northern part of the dungeon, a [[blood talisman]] or [[blood tiara]] is required for players to enter the ruins. Players may also access the altar through the [[blood rift]] in the [[Abyss]]. In this area, a nearby skeleton can be searched for a [[Tatty note (Sins of the Father)|tatty note]].

[[File:Darkness of Hallowvale - route to lab.png|thumb|right|upright|Route to the Meiyerditch Laboratories.]]
The entrance to the Meiyerditch Laboratory is in the house with the [[slashed tapestry]], which is south-east of the location you arrive at once exiting the [[Meiyerditch mine]]. 
There are various ways to get there:

* One of the fastest ways to reach the Meiyerditch Laboratories is to ask the closest [[Vyrewatch]] to be sent to the mines, and then exiting. Once you exit, follow the path to the house with the slashed tapestry and climb down the stairs to enter the Meiyerditch Laboratories (See image: "Route to the Meiyerditch Laboratories").
** To exit the mine immediately, players who haven't completed [[The Blood Moon Rises]] up until the final Lowerniel Drakan fight will need to equip three pieces of [[Vyre noble clothing]] when speaking with a [[Vampyre Juvinate]]. Otherwise, one must mine 15 [[daeyalt ore]] to exit; bring the best pickaxe you can use, or ask the [[Meiyerditch miner]]s for a spare [[bronze pickaxe]].
** Access to the bloodvelds is only possible after killing the [[mutated bloodveld]] that appears during the [[Sins of the Father]] quest, as otherwise the door will not open.

* After Sins of the Father, players can also do the following:
** Use a [[Hallowed crystal shard]] and exit the [[Hallowed Sepulchre]]. Run south and west to reach the [[cracked wall]], follow the path to the house with slashed tapestry, then climb down the stairs.
** Teleport to [[Edgeville]] or the [[Grand Exchange]], cross the wilderness ditch and run north to the [[Mage of Zamorak]]. Enter the [[Abyss]] and go to the [[blood rift]], being sure to select the true blood altar instead of the Kourend altar. While this is comparative to the 93 Agility shortcut in speed without having any requirements beyond quest completion, it carries the costly risk of losing your items to a player killer. It also has the downsides of draining your prayer to 0 and being skulled.
** Use a [[Drakan's medallion]] and teleport to [[Darkmeyer]]. Run north past the bank, east until you reach the entrance to the hallowed sepulchre, south along the main road, and finally west to reach the [[cracked wall]]. Follow the path to the house with slashed tapestry, climb down the stairs.
** Teleport to [[Canifis]], go down the [[Myreque Hideout]] trapdoor (south of [[Hair of the Dog]] Inn), go south through the secret wall, take the first cave east, travel directly south through the next cave entrance shortcut until you reach the Meiyerditch Laboratories cave system. This shortcut requires 93 Agility and 78 Mining along with a pickaxe the first time it is used.  The shortcut must first be cleared by bringing a pickaxe to the laboratory side of the shortcut specifically and clearing the shortcut's tunnel.  Subsequent uses just require 93 Agility and can be entered from either side. Alternatively, [[fairy ring]] code {{Fairycode|DLS}} can also be used to access the Myreque tunnels before the shortcut.

'''Neypotzli''' is a prison beneath [[Cam Torum]] that seals three powerful nagua known as the [[Moons of Peril]], and the shaman that summoned them. Created by the [[Old Ones]], the prison was sealed with water and earth runic energies, with [[Eyatlalli]], a nagua of earth and stream, being summoned to watch over the prison and reinforce the seals as needed.

The prison remained hidden for thousands of years until an earthquake caused a cave-in that revealed them; though the [[Imcando dwarves]] of [[Cam Torum]] initially attempted to cover it up, news eventually spread of its discovery. [[Civitas illa Fortis]], who wished to set up an archaeological dig in the newly-discovered ruins, attempted to make a deal with Cam Torum for access, involving expensive export deals and exclusive imports from the mainland kingdoms. After weeks of negotiations, the deal finally went through, allowing the [[Grand Museum]] to send [[Jessamine]] to lead the dig.

Accessing Neypotzli requires having gained access during the [[Perilous Moons]] quest, which acts as an introduction to the prison and the bosses. The area is not multi combat, but a dwarven cannon can be set up for Slayer tasks within the caverns.

===Antechamber===
The antechamber is the first area in which players reach upon entering Neypotzli, and contains three accessible entrances that are used to explore further into the prison.

The obsidian icosahedron in the centre is the key to the naguanil magic that keeps the Moons of Peril imprisoned, reshaping the seals as they attempt to break them. Right-clicking "Visual-effects" on it allows players with visual impairments to toggle whether they'd like to disable the colourful transition effects in the prison.

Additionally, murals depicting the Moons of Peril are also found here, with inscriptions written in the Old Ones' language. Whilst it cannot be seen in game, [[Jessamine]] roughly translates it as "Here in Neypotzli, by ??? of earth and streams, have these emissaries of ??? been sealed, ??? ??? ???."
